stories.headline: Putin admits oil deficit and adjusted fuel plans amid Ukrainian strikes on refineries
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has acknowledged a "certain deficit" of fuel in the country due to Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries. This admission marks the first time Putin has detailed the impact of Ukraine's deep-strike successes on Russia's fuel production. Ukraine has been carrying out drone attacks on Russian oil facilities, including a major refinery in southern Russia that was set on fire. In response, Putin has vowed to strengthen protection of oil facilities and boost fuel output to address the shortage. The Ukrainian strikes have hampered Russia's fuel production, leading to a notable deficit, prompting Putin to adjust the country's fuel plans. The attacks are part of an ongoing conflict between the two nations, with Ukraine continuing its heavy drone assault on Russian targets.

stories.headline: Rwanda: Can the 'Madman Theory' Oust the Tutsi From Their Historical Homelands?
stories.summary: Rwanda's historical conflicts between Hutu and Tutsi populations have deep roots. The division was formalized in the 1930s when Rwandans were required to declare their group identity, resulting in approximately 15% identifying as Tutsi, 84% as Hutu, and 1% as Twa. Tensions escalated in 1990 when the Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF), a Tutsi rebel group backed by Uganda, invaded Rwanda, killing customs guards and sparking a violent conflict. The RPF's goal was to oust President Habyarimana and establish a more democratic government. This led to the 1994 genocide, which shocked the world. The concept of the "madman theory," a political strategy of projecting irrationality to force negotiation, has been referenced in the context of Rwanda's conflicts, suggesting a potential application of this tactic to influence the Tutsi population's position in their historical homelands.

stories.headline: Zimbabwe: Top Lawyer Slams Justice Minister Ziyambi Over CAB3, Says He Is Pushing Proposed Legislation for Selfish Political Expediency
stories.summary: Zimbabwe's Justice Minister Ziyambi Ziyambi is facing criticism from a top lawyer, Jacqueline Sande-Kamanga, over the proposed Constitutional Amendment Number 3 Bill (CAB3). Sande-Kamanga accuses Ziyambi of pushing the legislation for selfish political expedience, undermining constitutionalism. Ziyambi claims the amendments aim to reduce political polarization and enhance constitutional coherence. The bill has sparked controversy, with opposition leader Chamisa stating that Ziyambi's address to Parliament reveals the ruling party's desperation. Ziyambi has announced plans to recall legislators for a special sitting to discuss the bill, despite Parliament being adjourned until July 7. The move has been met with resistance, with critics arguing that the amendments serve the interests of the ruling party rather than the nation. The debate surrounding CAB3 continues to escalate, with Ziyambi defending the proposed changes as necessary legal refinements.

stories.headline: As international enrollment falls, U.S. students face program cuts and higher prices
stories.summary: New international student enrollment at US institutions fell 17% in the fall 2025 semester, according to a recent report. Around 62% of institutions reported lower international student enrollment in both undergraduate and graduate programs compared to last year. The decline is largely attributed to federal actions to limit immigration, which have affected international students' decisions to enroll at US colleges and universities. Visa issuance and immigration challenges have also contributed to the decline, particularly at the graduate level. As a result, some colleges are reporting dramatic declines in enrollment among master's-level students. The decline in international enrollment may lead to program cuts and higher prices for US students, as institutions rely on international students to supplement their revenue. The trend is expected to continue, with federal policies and immigration challenges persisting.

stories.headline: Huawei Kirin 2026 Pro chip performance could match Apple A19
stories.summary: Huawei's upcoming Kirin 2026 Pro chip is expected to match the performance of Apple's A19 processor. The chip may be only 3% less efficient than the 3nm A19 Pro mobile SoC. Huawei will utilize the LogicFolding design concept for the Kirin 2026 Pro, enhancing its performance. The company is rumored to unveil new smartphones in July and August, with the Mate 90 series launch still expected in September. The Kirin 2026 Pro's performance is anticipated to be competitive with other high-end chips, including the Samsung Exynos 2600 and MediaTek Dimensity 9500, although it may still trail the A19 Pro. The chip's official launch is highly anticipated, with leaks and rumors suggesting a significant boost in performance for Huawei's upcoming devices.

stories.headline: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra: Bloomberg analyst tips likely Apple launch date
stories.summary: Bloomberg analyst Mark Gurman predicts the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra will be announced on either September 8 or September 9. The launch date speculation comes ahead of Apple's traditional September event, which will be the first keynote led by new CEO John Ternus. Gurman considers September 8 the most likely date, but notes that Apple may prefer a gap day after Labor Day on September 7. The iPhone 18 Pro models and the highly anticipated foldable iPhone Ultra are expected to debut at the event. While Apple has not confirmed the launch date, Gurman's prediction is based on the company's historical release patterns. The event is expected to bring significant news for Apple fans, marking a new era under Ternus' leadership.

stories.headline: Pokémon Champions Surpasses 10 Million Downloads Worldwide
stories.summary: Pokémon Champions has surpassed 10 million downloads worldwide, achieving this milestone just over a week after its mobile launch on June 17. The game is available for free download on the Nintendo eShop, Google Play, and the Apple App Store. To celebrate, 100 Fast Coupons will be given to all users until August 31. Pokémon Champions allows for cross-play between Nintendo Switch and mobile devices, enhancing the gaming experience. Additionally, new events and connectivity with Pokémon LEGENDS Z-A are active, further expanding the game's features. The game's rapid success demonstrates its popularity among Pokémon fans, and the distribution of commemorative coupons is a gesture of appreciation to its players. The milestone and subsequent celebration event are detailed on the game's official website.

stories.headline: SNK Unveils 'Art of Fighting: The Path of the Warrior R', a Remaster 30 Years in the Making
stories.summary: SNK Corporation has announced "The Path of the Warrior: Art of Fighting 3 R", a remastered version of the 1996 fighting game. The game is part of SNK's NEOGEO Premium Selection label and will be released on PC via Steam. This remaster optimizes graphics and systems for modern platforms, adding modern online play, rollback netcode, and full character balance changes. It also features a broader training mode and faster VS mode. The project is more than a simple reissue of the original arcade game, with significant updates to enhance the gaming experience. The release date has not been announced yet, with additional details to be revealed later. The remaster aims to modernize the classic arcade game while maintaining its original charm and high-freedom gameplay.

stories.headline: 2026 World Cup: Two African countries eliminated from tournament
stories.summary: Two African countries have been eliminated from the 2026 World Cup. The tournament, featuring 48 teams, has seen 17 nations eliminated after the group stage conclusion. Initially, 10 countries were confirmed out, with Curacao being the latest to exit after a 2-0 defeat to Ivory Coast. As of June 29, 2026, 32 nations have secured their places in the Round of 32, while 16 teams have been eliminated. The expanded tournament format has produced several confirmed qualifiers and eliminated teams before the final round of group-stage fixtures. With the group stage nearing its end, more teams are expected to be eliminated, narrowing down the competition for the remaining spots in the knockout stage.

stories.headline: Canada knocks South Africa out of World Cup, cruise to Round of 32
stories.summary: Canada defeated South Africa 1-0 in the Round of 32 of the FIFA World Cup 2026, with Stephen Eustaquio scoring the winning goal in stoppage time. The match seemed headed for extra time, but Eustaquio's 92nd-minute strike secured the victory for Canada. The win knocks South Africa out of the tournament. Canada's captain, Alphonso Davies, made his tournament debut after missing the group stage due to a hamstring injury. The match was closely contested, with South Africa putting in a strong defensive performance to keep Canada at bay for most of the game. Eustaquio's late goal lifted Canada to a dramatic 1-0 victory, advancing them to the next round of the World Cup. The win marks a significant milestone for Canada in the tournament.

stories.headline: "When we meet, we know why we meet" - French Women take different approach to first training camp
stories.summary: The French Women's national team has commenced their first training camp under Coach Cyril Burdet. Initially, Burdet had low expectations but was pleasantly surprised by the team's shape and performance during testing and training. He noted that the team is in better shape than expected. The team's approach to the camp is focused and intense, with Burdet emphasizing that their meetings are purpose-driven, aimed at training, improvement, and pushing themselves harder than they would at home. This mindset is a continuation of their approach over the last four years, where fun is balanced with a strong work ethic. The women's camp follows the men's first training camp, which concluded a day earlier. The team's performance and progress will be closely monitored as they prepare for upcoming competitions. Burdet's satisfaction with the team's condition is a positive sign for their future endeavors.

stories.headline: Knepp estate storks begin to nest in Guildford industrial estate
stories.summary: Storks from the Knepp Estate in Sussex have been spotted nesting in an industrial estate near Guildford, marking a significant milestone for the rewilding project. The Knepp Estate has been working to reintroduce White Storks to south-east England since 2016, aiming to establish a wild, breeding population of at least 50 pairs by 2030. The project, in partnership with the Roy Dennis Wildlife Foundation and others, has shown success, with the 2024 and 2025 breeding seasons yielding positive results. The sighting of storks nesting in Surrey indicates the birds are expanding their range, a promising sign for the project's goals. The White Stork Project involves several partners, including Knepp Castle Estate, private landowners, and Cotswold Wildlife Park, all working together to re-establish a thriving population of White Storks in the region.

stories.headline: Why the Delhi Gymkhana eviction should terrify every housing society and hospital in India If a perpetual lease and a High Court deferral can’t stop the state from seizing land on a whim, no institutional or private plot is safe.
stories.summary: The Delhi Gymkhana Club, a prestigious private institution, has been ordered to vacate its 27.3-acre premises in Lutyens' Delhi by the government. The club, which has a 1928 perpetual lease agreement, is fighting the eviction notice in the Delhi High Court. The government is invoking a public-purpose clause in the lease agreement to justify the eviction. The club's members, including politicians, business tycoons, and celebrities, are challenging the move. The dispute has sparked concerns that no institutional or private plot is safe from state seizure, despite court orders and perpetual leases. The case is the latest chapter in a long-running dispute between the government and the club over governance, finances, and use of prime public land in the national capital. The Delhi High Court is currently hearing the matter.

stories.headline: Courts should not be inclined to grant maintenance to wife if she is financially sound: Karnataka High Court Courts should not be inclined to grant maintenance merely on gendered assumptions that women are required to be maintained by men, particularly when the woman d
stories.summary: The Karnataka High Court has ruled that courts should not automatically grant maintenance to a wife simply because she is a woman, especially if she is financially sound and earns more than her husband. The court stated that maintenance cannot be awarded without examining the financial condition of both spouses. In a recent case, the court set aside an interim maintenance order in favor of a wife who earned Rs. 1,00,000 per month, nearly double her husband's income. The court held that maintenance can only be granted when the wife is unable to maintain herself according to the standard of living of her husband. This ruling emphasizes that maintenance decisions should be based on financial need, not gendered assumptions. The court's decision aims to ensure that maintenance is awarded fairly and reasonably.

stories.headline: Video: Fire At High Rise In Noida, AC blast Suspected Upon receiving information, around half a dozen fire tenders rushed to the spot and firefighting operations were immediately launched.
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in a high-rise building in Noida's Sector 119, specifically at Aranya Society. The fire started on the 22nd floor after an air conditioner allegedly exploded in a flat. Six fire tenders rushed to the scene and launched firefighting operations. The blaze quickly spread, sending thick black smoke and flames into the sky, causing panic among residents. People evacuated the building to safety as the fire threatened nearby apartments. Fortunately, no casualties have been reported so far, according to the police. Firefighting operations are ongoing, with multiple fire tenders working to bring the situation under control. The prompt response from the fire brigade helped prevent further damage and ensured the safety of the residents. The cause of the fire is suspected to be an AC blast, which is being investigated.

stories.headline: Massive fire breaks out at high-rise flat in Noida's sector 119; 6 fire tenders deployed NOIDA: A fire broke out in a flat at Aranya Society in Sector 119 on Monday.Six fire service tenders were rushed to the spot, and firefighting operati
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in a flat at Aranya Society in Noida's Sector 119 on Monday. The fire department received a call around 8:50 am and immediately dispatched six fire tenders, along with police and an ambulance, to the spot. Firefighting operations are currently underway. The fire is believed to have started on the 22nd floor and may have been caused by an air conditioner explosion. Fortunately, no injuries have been reported. The swift response from the fire department and emergency services helped to contain the situation. The cause of the fire is being investigated, but initial reports suggest it was an accident rather than a deliberate act. The fire has been brought under control, and further details are awaited.

stories.headline: Easing geopolitics, mega listings like Jio, and market recovery are boosting IPOs
stories.summary: India's IPO market is experiencing a boost due to easing geopolitics, mega listings, and market recovery. Reliance Jio and NSE are among the companies expected to list soon, with SEBI considering easing norms for large companies. The proposed changes include reduced public offer requirements and extended timelines for meeting minimum public shareholding, addressing potential share oversupply concerns. Easing geopolitical tensions in West Asia are positively impacting investor sentiment, encouraging more companies to pursue public listings. With around Rs 3.5-4 lakh crore of IPOs in the pipeline, factors such as geopolitical stability and the return of foreign investors are key for an uptick in IPOs. Analysts believe successful listings could boost market participation, and several IPOs are scheduled for launch, sparking optimism for a revival in the primary market.

stories.headline: Discover what's driving the H2 2026 IPO boom in India
stories.summary: India's primary market is set to break records in 2026 with an unprecedented IPO pipeline exceeding Rs 2.5 lakh crore. The country is witnessing a historic IPO boom, driven by robust domestic liquidity, rising retail participation, and improving governance. Marquee companies such as Jio, NSE, Flipkart, and top unicorns are readying for listings, solidifying India's position as a vibrant IPO destination. The IPO momentum is expected to continue, with an estimated $20 billion in fundraising. Key trends and major listings are expected to shape the market, with companies like CARS24 also planning to list on the bourses. The strong IPO pipeline is a testament to India's growing capital markets, with 2026 poised to be a significant year for the country's primary market. The listings are expected to drive growth and investment in the country.

stories.headline: The 2026 IPO Boom: Jio, NSE, and the Resurgence of India's Primary Market
stories.summary: India's primary market is expected to see a significant surge in 2026, with projected IPO fundraising of nearly Rs 1.77 lakh crore. The pipeline includes notable listings from companies like Jio Platforms, NSE, Zepto, and SBI Mutual Fund, which are gearing up for public issues in the second half of 2026. The IPO market has been sluggish so far in 2026 due to weak market sentiment and uncertainty. However, upcoming IPOs from NSE and Reliance Jio could add up to ₹20 lakh crore in value, reshaping India's markets. Investors are tracking issue size, OFS details, price bands, and dates for these listings. The recent dual filing event, the biggest in a decade, has sparked interest in the market, with these IPOs leading India's biggest listing wave in 2026. Equirus Capital's projection suggests a strong year ahead for India's primary market.

stories.headline: From geopolitics to AI to lifestyle, get the views from the best in the world
stories.summary: The world is undergoing a triple transition in AI, energy systems, and geopolitics, all happening simultaneously. Leaders in the public and private sectors must consider the energy system and international politics to deliver on AI's promises. This convergence presents risks and opportunities for businesses, requiring careful management. In 2025, the pursuit of profit drove the AI race, outweighing geopolitical concerns. Recent developments highlight the need for regulation, ethics, and responsible business practices in AI. Reuters and other news outlets provide in-depth coverage of AI breakthroughs, technology trends, and global impact, offering a comprehensive view of how technology is shaping the world. The intersection of AI, energy, and geopolitics demands attention from leaders and businesses to navigate the challenges and opportunities arising from these interconnected transitions.

stories.headline: Sensex Declines 247 Points, Nifty Trades With Marginal Gains As Renewed Iran-US Tensions Weigh On Investor Sentiment
stories.summary: The Sensex declined 247 points to 76,853, a 0.32 percent drop, in early trade due to renewed US-Iran tensions. The Nifty 50, however, opened 5 points higher at 24,061. As the day progressed, the Sensex fell 372.10 points, or 0.48 percent, to 76,728.37, while the Nifty dropped 109.75 points, or 0.46 percent, to 23,946.25. The decline in benchmark indices was attributed to fresh hostilities between the US and Iran, which revived concerns over geopolitical risk and higher crude oil prices, dampening investor sentiment across sectors. The tensions led to a cautious approach by investors, resulting in marginal gains for the Nifty earlier in the day, but ultimately closing lower. The market's performance was influenced by global events, highlighting the impact of geopolitical tensions on investor sentiment and market volatility.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty opened in red, then recovered
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex initially declined 63.65 points to 77,047.63 but later recovered. The Nifty50 also followed a similar trend, opening in red before rebounding. The recovery was driven by various market factors. Meanwhile, the Government of India is set to sell a 2% stake in Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) via an offer-for-sale on June 24-25, with a greenshoe option for an additional 1% stake. Global cues were mixed, with US stock futures climbing after a halt on US strikes in Iran. The market's sharp turnaround in the second half of the session was attributed to several factors, leading to a recovery in the Sensex and Nifty50. The sale of IRFC stake is expected to take place on June 24-25, as announced by the Government of India.

stories.headline: Sensex falls 50 points, Nifty above 24,050; Eternal, Sun Pharma, TechM rise 1%
stories.summary: The Sensex fell 50 points, while the Nifty remained above 24,050. During Monday's session, the Sensex dropped 45 points to 77,055, and the Nifty 50 gained nearly 6 points to 24,061.75. Broader markets declined, with the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 indices falling 0.06% each. Earlier, the BSE Sensex opened 180 points higher at 80,396 and surged to an intra-day high of 80,661 before losing momentum. The indices later erased losses, with the Sensex trading 29.75 points higher at 77,123.82 and the Nifty gaining 20.80 points to 24,123.65. Stocks like Eternal, Sun Pharma, and TechM rose 1%. The market rally was supported by lower crude oil prices and buying in select sectors, including pharma, which lifted the Nifty to 24,127 and the Sensex to a 85-point gain.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today: Sensex Up 63 Points, Nifty Above 24,090 In Early Trade
stories.summary: The Indian stock market opened higher, with the BSE Sensex rising 63.43 points to 77,163.90 and the Nifty 50 gaining 39.40 points to 24,095.40 in early trade. This comes after a decline on May 26, 2026, when the Sensex closed down 479.26 points at 76,009.70 and the Nifty closed down 118 points at 23,913.70. Previously, a break below 23,920 was expected to lead to a target of 60 to 70 points down. The Nifty had reclaimed 24,100 on April 15, 2026, but volatility was high due to expiry day. Currently, the Nifty 50 is expected to consolidate within the 25,900-26,100 range, with a potential upside if it breaks above 26,100. The market is showing positive movement, with global cues also being positive.

stories.headline: Risks of a tumbling house and apartment property market The government’s decision to use policy to let more air out of the housing market could push prices too hard.
stories.summary: The government's decision to implement policies to slow down the housing market may push prices too low, especially after higher interest rates have already made the market unstable. A few months of price falls could lead to a downward trajectory that is difficult to reverse. High mortgage rates, insurance, property taxes, and maintenance costs are contributing to low home affordability, with foreclosure rates potentially quadrupling by 2025. Climate-related expenses and resiliency requirements are also influencing buyers' decisions, with billion-dollar weather disasters on the rise. As a result, land values, insurance availability, and development economics may be reshaped, leading to changes in geographic growth patterns across various markets. The housing market outlook for 2026 has been slashed due to price drops, geographic weakness, and mortgage rate shocks.

stories.headline: Coventry gigafactory may be downsized, CEO admits Owner Steve Rigby says he does not think the site "will be at the full scale we planned".
stories.summary: Coventry's planned gigafactory may be downsized, according to its CEO Steve Rigby. Rigby stated that he does not think the site will be at the full scale initially planned. The factory, intended as a "centre of excellence for battery technology, advanced manufacturing and clean energy", was set to be built at Coventry Airport, which is scheduled to close in 2026 to make way for the project. However, the plans are now in limbo as the proposal faces expiry. Rigby cited global competition, particularly from China, as a significant factor affecting the project's scale. The downsizing announcement raises uncertainty about the future of the gigafactory, which was expected to be a major development for the area.

stories.headline: Chiyoda signs an Enterprise Framework Agreement for engineering services with Shell Chiyoda Corporation has signed an Enterprise Framework Agreement (EFA) for engineering and procurement services with Shell Global Solutions International, to su
stories.summary: Chiyoda Corporation has signed an Enterprise Framework Agreement (EFA) with Shell Global Solutions International for engineering and procurement services to support potential future projects globally. The agreement aims to facilitate Shell's access to Chiyoda's technical expertise as new energy development needs arise. This partnership builds on the duo's existing 50-year collaboration, where Chiyoda has supported Shell on major projects worldwide. The agreement is intended to help Shell projects start more quickly while improving cost certainty, schedule certainty, and execution predictability. Chiyoda will provide engineering and procurement services for potential future projects worldwide under the agreement, further strengthening the company's long-standing relationship with Shell. The deal enables Chiyoda to lend its expertise to Shell's global projects, solidifying their trusted collaboration.

stories.headline: Chairman Of Luxury Department Store Operator Shinsegae Enters Billionaire Ranks Amid South Korea’s Stock Surge Shinsegae heiress and company chairman is benefitting from the AI boom that’s made retail investors wealthy enough to splurge on luxury goods.
stories.summary: Shinsegae Group chairman and heiress Chung Yoo-kyung has entered the billionaire ranks amid South Korea's stock market surge driven by the artificial intelligence boom. The company's shares have risen 220% year-to-date, outperforming even Samsung, despite having no direct ties to AI. The growth is attributed to the increased wealth of retail investors, who are splurging on luxury goods sold at Shinsegae's department stores. Flush with newfound wealth, these investors are driving luxury spending, adding to the company's growth momentum. Shinsegae has also attracted investors with its shareholder returns, including the retirement of 200,000 treasury shares and a raised annual cash dividend. Chung Yoo-kyung is pushing for a spin-off of Shinsegae Department Store from Shinsegae Group, led by her older brother Chairman Chung Yong-jin. The company's strong performance has propelled Chung Yoo-kyung to billionaire status.

stories.headline: Google Loses Two More AI Researchers to Anthropic – NaturalNews.com
stories.summary: Two leading AI researchers at Google are leaving to join rival Anthropic. The researchers, Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel, are key contributors to the company's AI development. This move is part of a larger trend, with DeepMind engineers nearly 11 times more likely to leave Google for Anthropic than the reverse. The brain drain is significant for Google, which is attempting to boost collaboration and streamline its AI work. The departure of top talent may impact Google's ability to compete in the AI space. Anthropic, a rival AI company, is gaining experienced researchers, potentially strengthening its position in the industry. The loss of Adler and Pritzel follows other recent departures, highlighting the challenges Google faces in retaining top AI talent.

stories.headline: Alternatives to OpenAI, Anthropic: With US prime AI off the table, India opts for fine China Chinese open-source models
stories.summary: India is shifting its AI strategy due to export pressure, opting for Chinese open-source models as alternatives to US-based OpenAI and Anthropic. Chinese models, such as Zhipu's GLM 5.2, have gained popularity among Indian startups and enterprises due to their lower costs. These models are now being fine-tuned for use in large enterprises, reducing dependence on top-dollar US AI projects. The move comes as Chinese AI startups, like Z.ai, are making waves with powerful and inexpensive models, challenging the dominance of US companies in the industry. Indian enterprises are adapting these models to suit their needs, potentially making India's AI strategy less reliant on US-based technologies. This shift may also promote the development of AI systems that can comprehend India's linguistic diversity.

stories.headline: No other headlines are provided to select from, only two are given.
stories.summary: Multiple news sources are available for accessing current events, including CNN.com for US and global news, ABC News Live for 24/7 live coverage, and MailOnline for UK and international headlines. BBC News offers a wide range of topics, including world news, entertainment, climate, business, science, technology, and health, providing trusted perspectives from various regions. These platforms allow users to stay updated on the latest news and developments. Additionally, initiatives like TOI Young Leaders aim to foster skills such as leadership, creativity, and communication in children. With numerous sources at their disposal, individuals can choose the outlets that best suit their interests and preferences for staying informed about local and global events. These news sources cater to diverse audiences, providing comprehensive coverage of various topics.
